name: Environmental Chemistry
tagline: Pollutant fate, atmospheric chemistry, and remediation strategies.
seo_title: Environmental Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Environmental Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in air and water pollution, climate chemistry, PFAS and remediation.

definition.lead: Environmental chemistry studies chemicals in air, water and soil: where they come from, how they move and change, and what they do to living things.
definition.body: It explains the ozone hole, acid rain, smog, climate forcing and the fate of pesticides, plastics and 'forever chemicals'. Its measurements underpin environmental law and the cleanup of polluted sites.

timeline.title: The Great Smog
timeline.text: A smog from coal burning kills thousands of people in London.
timeline.why: Led to the UK's Clean Air Act.

timeline.title: Minamata disease
timeline.text: Methylmercury poisoning from industrial waste is identified in Minamata, Japan.
timeline.why: Showed how pollutants concentrate up food chains.

timeline.title: Silent Spring
timeline.text: Rachel Carson documents the effects of pesticides.

timeline.title: The EPA
timeline.text: The United States creates the Environmental Protection Agency.
timeline.why: Environmental chemistry became the basis of regulation.

timeline.title: CFCs and ozone
timeline.text: Mario Molina and Sherwood Rowland warn that CFCs can destroy stratospheric ozone.
timeline.why: A molecular threat to the ozone layer.

timeline.title: The ozone hole
timeline.text: Joe Farman, Brian Gardiner and Jonathan Shanklin report severe ozone loss over Antarctica.
timeline.why: Turned the warning into hard evidence.

timeline.title: The Montreal Protocol
timeline.text: Countries agree to phase out ozone-depleting substances.
timeline.why: Widely seen as the most successful environmental treaty.

timeline.title: Nobel Prize for ozone
timeline.text: Awarded to Paul Crutzen, Mario Molina and Sherwood Rowland.
timeline.why: Atmospheric chemistry recognized at the highest level.

timeline.title: The Stockholm Convention
timeline.text: A global treaty to eliminate or restrict persistent organic pollutants is adopted.

timeline.title: A PFAS listed
timeline.text: PFOS is added to the Stockholm Convention.
timeline.why: Forever chemicals came under global control.
